flood.title: Flood Emergency Checklist
dos: Move to higher ground / upper floors immediately
Keep emergency kit ready (torch, water, dry food, medicines, documents)
Keep mobile phone charged and follow official alerts
Turn off electricity mains if water is entering the building
donts: Do not walk or drive through moving flood water
Do not touch downed power lines or standing water near them
Do not re-enter flooded buildings until declared safe

cyclone.title: Cyclone Emergency Checklist
dos: Secure loose outdoor objects (furniture, hoardings, antennas)
Stay indoors, away from windows, in the strongest part of the building
Keep an emergency kit and identify nearest official shelter
Follow IMD and local disaster authority warnings closely
donts: Do not go outside during the 'eye' of the storm — winds return suddenly
Do not travel unless officially cleared

landslide.title: Landslide Emergency Checklist
dos: Move away and uphill immediately if you notice cracks, tilting trees, or ground bulging
Report warning signs to local authorities
Avoid river valleys and unstable slopes during/after heavy rain
donts: Do not stay in low-lying areas near slopes during continuous heavy rain
Do not ignore new cracks in walls or ground

lightning.title: Lightning Emergency Checklist
dos: Move indoors or into a hard-topped vehicle immediately when thunder is heard
Stay indoors for at least 30 minutes after the last thunderclap
donts: Do not stay in open fields, near isolated trees, metal fences, or water bodies
Do not use corded phones or plumbing during a lightning storm
